# Requirements Document: Payment time limits

## Introduction

An order item waiting for payment carries a payment time limit.  When the
limit passes and no successful payment covers the item, the item is removed
and any payment still pending for it fails.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Payment/TimeLimit.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Payment/TimeLimit.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-306

**User Story:** As an airline, I want unpaid order items removed when their payment time limit passes, so that seats and services are not held for customers who do not pay.

**Rule:** WHEN an order item's payment time limit passes with no SUCCESSFUL payment covering it THE SYSTEM SHALL remove the item and mark FAILED every PENDING payment that covers it. (Lean: `expireUnpaid`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an order item's payment time limit has passed and no SUCCESSFUL payment covers it THE SYSTEM SHALL remove the item, cancelling every service of it that the delivery status table lets end, so that none of those services is live afterwards.
   - ONE-306.1, proven: proven theorem `expireUnpaid_removes`; example `lateRedirectCapture`; example `unpaidAtTimeLimit`
2. WHEN an order item is removed at its payment time limit THE SYSTEM SHALL mark FAILED every PENDING payment that covers it.
   - ONE-306.2, proven: proven theorem `expireUnpaid_fails_pending`; example `lateRedirectCapture`; example `unpaidAtTimeLimit`
3. IF a SUCCESSFUL payment covers an order item THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL not remove the item at a payment time limit.
   - ONE-306.3, proven: proven theorem `expireUnpaid_keeps_paid`; example `unpaidAtTimeLimit`
4. WHILE an order item's payment time limit has not passed THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the item unchanged.
   - ONE-306.4, proven: proven theorem `expireUnpaid_keeps_before_limit`; example `unpaidAtTimeLimit`
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL not keep an unpaid order item in the order indefinitely.
   - ONE-306.5, open: open theorem `unpaid_item_removed_eventually`; counterexample `noTimeLimit`
6. WHEN an order item is removed at its payment time limit THE SYSTEM SHALL leave none of its services holding value.
   - ONE-306.6, open: open theorem `removed_item_holds_no_value`; counterexample `removalStatuses`

#### Open question on ONE-306.5

> An unpaid order item does not stay in the order indefinitely: from some
> instant on, the time limit rule removes it.
>
> Open question for the business.  The rule removes an item only when its
> payment time limit passes, and the guide lets an airline create an order item
> without one.  The ARMI guidance expects a limit on every unpaid item, while the
> EASD guide says a missing limit only means the airline gave no advice.  An item
> without a limit is never removed and holds its services with nothing paid; the
> example `noTimeLimit` shows it a year after the order was created.  May
> an unpaid order item exist without a payment time limit, and if so, may it stay
> unpaid indefinitely?

#### Open question on ONE-306.6

> An order item removed at its payment time limit holds no value: none of its
> services holds value afterwards.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide says such an item is removed and
> names no resulting statuses.  If its services become REMOVED, none holds value
> under every reading of the guide.  If they become EXPIRED, whether they hold
> value is itself unsettled: under the cautious reading an expired service holds
> value, so the removed item stays active and keeps its order opened.  If they
> become REMOVED HOLD VALUE, they hold value under every reading.  The example
> `removalStatuses` shows all three.  Which delivery status does an item's
> service take when its payment time limit passes unpaid?
